newsitem.title: USA: In Home Health sees higher FY97 revenues.
newsitem.headline: In Home Health sees higher FY97 revenues.

text.p: In Home Health Inc officials said Thursday the company hopes to report revenues higher than those posted in fiscal 1996 by the time the current fiscal year ends in September.
Chief Executive Officer Mark Gildea told Reuters the company expected fiscal 1997 revenues in excess of the $125 million achieved in 1996.
"We're looking at beating the $125 million," Gildea said.
Gildea declined to say whether the company would reach the $130 million total revenues posted in fiscal 1995.

Meanwhile, asked after the home health care services provider's annual meeting if the company expected an operating profit in fiscal 1997, Treasurer Kari Schell said, "We hope to and we're working very hard to do that."
Schell added that an analysts' projection of a $0.12 loss per share for fiscal 1997 was slightly pessimistic.
"It's probably reasonable or slightly low, slightly pessimistic," Schell said of the loss projected by First Call.
Schell also said the company was considering consolidating its branch office operations and cited a 19-percent reduction in corporate staff over the last six months.
Gildea also said he expected to obtain Medicare certification for the company's hospice program for 17 or 18 of its 20 markets by the end of fiscal 1997.
Hospice revenues were $3.8 million in 1996 and about $2.3 million in the first quarter of 1997, the company said.
"We could have substantial business (in the hospice unit) if we continue at the growth rate we're at," Gildea said.
Gildea told shareholders the company would increase the number of branch offices offering cardiology services from the current three to 13 by the end of the fiscal year and to 19 by December 31.
